paraphrase: Brahman, without beginning or end, whose essence is the Word (śabda-tattva), the imperishable (akṣara), appears (vivartate) in the form of things; from it the unfolding of the world proceeds.

original.text: anādinidhanaṃ brahma śabdatattvaṃ yad akṣaram | vivartate 'rthabhāvena prakriyā jagato yataḥ ||

paraphrase: The wise call grammar the nearest to that Brahman, the highest of austerities, the first among the limbs of the Veda.

paraphrase: It is the straight path to that supreme essence (rasa) of speech which has taken on divisions — the most holy light.

paraphrase: There is no cognition in the world in which the word does not figure; all knowledge shines as if pierced through by the word.

original.text: na so 'sti pratyayo loke yaḥ śabdānugamād ṛte | anuviddham iva jñānaṃ sarvaṃ śabdena bhāsate ||

paraphrase: If the eternal word-nature (vāg-rūpatā) of awareness were to depart, light would not illumine, for it is that which makes recognition (pratyavamarśa) possible.

paraphrase: Words alone are the basis of the truths about meanings and activities; there is no understanding of the truth of words without grammar.

paraphrase: It (grammar) is the door to liberation, the medicine for the impurities of speech, the purifier of all sciences; it shines as the science over the sciences.

original.text: tad dvāram apavargasya vāṅmalānāṃ cikitsitam | pavitraṃ sarvavidyānām adhividyaṃ prakāśate ||

paraphrase: The Veda (trayī), with its many fords and divisions, is the supreme station of this wondrous speech that is vaikharī, madhyamā and paśyantī.

paraphrase: This is the first rung on the ladder to perfection; this is the straight royal road for those who seek liberation.

paraphrase: It is the one that has been handed down (in the Veda); resting on its different powers, though not separate from those powers, it exists as if separate.

paraphrase: Depending on its time-power (kāla-śakti), onto which divisions are superimposed, the six modifications beginning with birth become the sources of all the varieties of being.

paraphrase: A matter inferred with effort by skilful reasoners is explained quite otherwise by others more skilled.

paraphrase: For those in whom light has dawned and whose minds are unclouded, knowledge of past and future is no different from perception.

paraphrase: Of that one which is the seed of all, this manifold existence is in the form of the enjoyer, the enjoyed and the enjoyment.

paraphrase: Those who know words recognize two 'words' in utterances: one is the cause (the sound, nimitta) of words, the other is applied to the meaning (the sphoṭa).

paraphrase: As light residing in the fire-sticks is the cause of other lights, so the word residing in the intellect is the separate cause of the heard sounds.

paraphrase: The Veda is the means of attaining it and its likeness (anukāra); though one, it has been handed down by the great seers as if of many paths, in many recensions.
notes: Vākyapadīya numbering follows K. A. Subramania Iyer's edition; W. Rau's edition numbers kāṇḍa 1 differently after about v. 30, so the locator may need conversion.

paraphrase: There are no letters in the word and no parts in the letters; there is no real separation of words from the sentence.

paraphrase: In the Veda is taught the truth and purification: a knowledge whose source is the one word (Oṃ), joined with the form of the praṇava, opposed to no doctrine.

paraphrase: The word (sphoṭa) is ascertained in the intellect when the sounds have planted their seeds in it and it has matured through repetition, together with the last sound; the sphoṭa has no sequence, but appears as if sequential because the sounds that manifest it come in sequence.

paraphrase: As a reflection situated elsewhere seems to follow the movement of the water, so the sphoṭa seems to take on the properties (length, speed) of the sounds that manifest it.
notes: Verse not fixed: located by content in kāṇḍa 1 (from memory); Vākyapadīya numbering follows K. A. Subramania Iyer's edition; W. Rau's edition numbers kāṇḍa 1 differently after about v. 30, so the locator may need conversion.

paraphrase: This speech is the consciousness (saṃjñā) of beings in saṃsāra, within and without; consciousness in all species does not go beyond it; it moves embodied beings to all their activities, and when it departs a being is seen to be without awareness, like a log or a wall.
notes: Verse not fixed: located by content in kāṇḍa 1 (from memory); Vākyapadīya numbering follows K. A. Subramania Iyer's edition; W. Rau's edition numbers kāṇḍa 1 differently after about v. 30, so the locator may need conversion.

paraphrase: Therefore the refinement of words (śabda-saṃskāra) is the attainment of the supreme self; one who knows the truth of its working attains the immortal Brahman.
notes: Verse not fixed: located by content in kāṇḍa 1 (from memory); Vākyapadīya numbering follows K. A. Subramania Iyer's edition; W. Rau's edition numbers kāṇḍa 1 differently after about v. 30, so the locator may need conversion.

paraphrase: Those who know the Veda know this (world) as a transformation (pariṇāma) of the word; this universe first evolved from the Vedic metres (chandas).
notes: Verse not fixed: located by content in kāṇḍa 1 (from memory); Vākyapadīya numbering follows K. A. Subramania Iyer's edition; W. Rau's edition numbers kāṇḍa 1 differently after about v. 30, so the locator may need conversion.

paraphrase: The logicians hold many different views of the sentence: the verb; the collection of words; the universal residing in the collection; the one partless word; the sequence; the unity grasped by the mind; the first word; each word separately needing the others.
notes: Vākyapadīya numbering follows K. A. Subramania Iyer's edition; W. Rau's edition numbers kāṇḍa 1 differently after about v. 30, so the locator may need conversion.

paraphrase: When the meanings of the separate words are grasped, a flash of understanding (pratibhā) different from them arises; that is called the meaning of the sentence, brought about by the word-meanings. It cannot be described to others as 'this is it'; it is established in each one's own experience, and even its possessor cannot define it; it fuses the meanings together and appears as their object.
notes: Vākyapadīya numbering follows K. A. Subramania Iyer's edition; W. Rau's edition numbers kāṇḍa 1 differently after about v. 30, so the locator may need conversion.

paraphrase: No one goes beyond pratibhā in knowing what is to be done; all the world takes it as authoritative, and even animals act by it: who teaches the cuckoo to sing in spring, or creatures to build nests, feed, love, hate and swim? It arises from nature, from conduct, from practice, from yoga, from unseen merit, or is conferred by the special ones — six kinds.
notes: Range recalled with moderate confidence; Vākyapadīya numbering follows K. A. Subramania Iyer's edition; W. Rau's edition numbers kāṇḍa 1 differently after about v. 30, so the locator may need conversion.

paraphrase: The closing verses tell the history of the grammar: Vyāḍi's Saṃgraha declined; Patañjali's Mahābhāṣya was composed; when it too fell into neglect among dry reasoners, Candrācārya and others, receiving the tradition from a mountain region, made it spread again in many branches.

paraphrase: (Jāti-samuddeśa) Words denote universals; the universal is the true part of each thing and the individuals the unreal part; differentiated by its relata, Being itself (sattā) is called 'cow' and the rest, and in it all words have their rest — the great universal is Brahman.
notes: Section-level reference; verse numbers not fixed. Vākyapadīya numbering follows K. A. Subramania Iyer's edition; W. Rau's edition numbers kāṇḍa 1 differently after about v. 30, so the locator may need conversion.

paraphrase: (Dravya-samuddeśa) Self, thing, own nature, body and reality are synonyms of 'substance' (dravya), and it is held to be eternal; as gold, apart from its passing forms, is what the words 'bracelet' and the rest finally denote, so the Real, apart from its unreal forms, is what all words denote.
notes: Section-level reference. Vākyapadīya numbering follows K. A. Subramania Iyer's edition; W. Rau's edition numbers kāṇḍa 1 differently after about v. 30, so the locator may need conversion.

paraphrase: (Sambandha-samuddeśa) When words are uttered, three things are understood — the speaker's cognition, the outer object and the word's own form; their relation (fitness, yogyatā) is fixed and eternal, not made by anyone.
notes: Section-level reference. Vākyapadīya numbering follows K. A. Subramania Iyer's edition; W. Rau's edition numbers kāṇḍa 1 differently after about v. 30, so the locator may need conversion.

paraphrase: (Kāla-samuddeśa) Time is the one, eternal, all-pervading power by which things are measured, which like a controller of a water-wheel or a wire-puller moves all things into appearance and disappearance; it is the independent power (svātantrya) of the Word-Brahman.
